title: Integral Brown hypotheses over finite or separably closed base fields
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ a finite intermediate extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ be its condensed ring of integers [def-sfb-padic-integers-condensed-ring]. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Assume that $k$ is finite or separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. Then the full Brown bundle $\operatorname{BrownHypothesesFor}(\Lambda,X)$ [lem-sfb-brown-hypotheses-criterion] holds, with the finite constant-model constructibility convention [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. In particular the bounded constructible finite-Tor objects are compact in their replete localizing closure; this assertion retains the additional hypothesis on $k$.

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of the finite-type structure map over Spec k makes X compact. Separatedness makes X quasi-separated. A finite constant-model constructible sheaf therefore has one finite stratification. On each stratum a finite constant local model is locally finitely presented. Transport local finite presentation across the canonical coefficient isomorphism, using extension of scalars isomorphic to restriction along its inverse. This proves ordinary constructibility in the sense used by the upstream Ext-bound theorem.

The characteristic identity ringChar k = p gives invertibility of ell. Apply the integral uniform constructible Ext-bound theorem with exactly the retained disjunction that k is finite or separably closed. For each source C it supplies an integer d such that every map from C in degree zero to N in single degree n is zero whenever n <= d, uniformly over constructible N. For q > -d one has -q < d, hence -q <= d. The canonical shift isomorphism N[0][q] is isomorphic to the single complex in degree -q. Postcomposition with this isomorphism identifies the desired Hom group with a zero Hom group, so it is subsingleton. No nonnegativity of d or nonzero-source assumption is needed.

Apply the reverse implication of the integral Brown-versus-Ext equivalence to these shifted-Hom bounds. It supplies the entire Brown bundle, including ambient structure, thickness, essential smallness, compactness and generation. The original arbitrary-field assertion is not used.
